items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: And then I played with the Symphony too, we did “Porgy and Bess” and another Gershwin thing.

ctx.x: So they gave me a couple of months to finish the tour and settle my affairs, and then I went in the Army I think March ’57 and then I got out New Year’s Eve in 1958. So it took a big chunk out which I regretted. I mean I think something could have happened to my career faster had I had that opportunity then. But actually my time in the service was mostly in Europe with the Seventh Army Symphony and we played a couple of soldier shows which are like Broadway shows that they send around to the different Kacernes ©…

they call them in Germany, and then we had a jazz show, an 18-piece jazz band that did six months over there. And I couldn’t have been any more fortunate. Along with myself it was Eddie Harris and Leo Wright and Don Ellis and Cedar Walton. So it was really playing with good musicians and also the outside playing — we used to go to Heidelberg and play at The Cave, it was a jazz joint there. And then I played with the Symphony too, we did “Porgy and Bess” and another Gershwin thing. So it wasn’t time wasted, it was…
